articles.headline: OFAC Issues Amended Iran-related General License for International Development Bank for Investment and Finance
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Iran General License FF-1, titled "Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance."

This amended general license, effective October 29, 2026, replaces and supersedes the previous General License FF. It specifically authorizes the wind-down of transactions involving the International Development Bank for Investment and Finance, also known as Iraq Development Bank, and certain majority-owned entities through December 1, 2026.
The new license also stipulates that payments to blocked persons must be made into blocked accounts.

articles.region: North Korea, Democratic Republic of the Congo
articles.headline: OFAC Designates Individuals and Entities for North Korea IT Worker Schemes and DRC Destabilization
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new designations targeting individuals and an entity involved in North Korean government-run IT worker schemes and actions related to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

Among the North Korea-related designations, OFAC sanctioned individuals like Ilya Aleksandrovich Boykov, Han Yu Song, Kim Hyo Dong, and Kim Ki Hyok, all linked to facilitating illicit financial transactions or leading IT worker delegations for North Korea. The entity First Financial and Technical Development Center was also added to the SDN list.

For the Democratic Republic of the Congo, OFAC designated the Ministry of Defence of the Republic of Rwanda and Zigama Credit and Savings Society for their role in facilitating Rwanda's support for the M23 movement in eastern DRC.

articles.headline: Extreme Networks Settles with OFAC for $1.5 Million Over Russia Sanctions Violations
body: Extreme Networks, Inc., a North Carolina-based cloud networking solutions provider, has agreed to pay $1,529,685 to settle potential civil liability for nine apparent violations of Ukraine-/Russia-Related Sanctions Regulations.

Between September 2018 and March 2022, Extreme Networks exported networking equipment and related services from the United States to Joint Stock Company Moskovskiy Mashinostroitelniy Zavod Avangard (MMZA), a Russian defense manufacturer. MMZA was deemed a blocked person due to its majority ownership by designated JSC Concern Almaz Antey, even though MMZA itself was not on the SDN list until June 2022.

OFAC determined that the apparent violations were egregious but voluntarily self-disclosed. The settlement emphasizes the importance of sanctions-related diligence during acquisitions, vigilance regarding sanctions risks, and adequate oversight of foreign operations.

articles.headline: OFAC Amends FAQs on Blocking, Rejecting Transactions, and Filing Reports
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has amended 11 of its Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) concerning blocking and rejecting transactions and filing reports with OFAC.

The revised FAQs, numbered 10, 32 through 36, 41, 42, 49, 50, and 53, are part of OFAC's ongoing review of its published guidance to ensure information remains current. The updates clarify when financial institutions must freeze funds versus rejecting prohibited transactions, and address reporting procedures, deadlines, and required documentation.

Key changes include emphasizing that initial blocking and rejected-transaction reports are generally due within 10 business days and must be submitted through the OFAC Reporting System (ORS) with supporting documentation.

articles.headline: OFAC Issues Iran and Russia-related General Licenses, Removes Belarus and North Korea Designations
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related and Russia-related General Licenses, alongside designations removals pertaining to Belarus and North Korea.

Specifically, OFAC issued Iran General License GG, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving Karnakis and Karnakis, and Iran General License HH, authorizing wind-down activities, limited safety and environmental transactions, and the offloading of cargo involving certain persons or vessels blocked on October 21, 2026.
The action also included amendments to Frequently Asked Questions and removals from the sanctions lists for certain entities and individuals related to Belarus and North Korea.

body: The Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued designations under the Protecting American Intellectual Property Act of 2022 (PAIPA) and released associated General Licenses.

Three Chinese entities have been added to OFAC's Non-SDN Menu-Based Sanctions List: Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase I Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership (a.k.a. Miracle Plus RMB Fund I), Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Zhiyuan Enterprise Management Center Limited Partnership, and Beijing Qiji Chuangtan Phase II Venture Capital Center Limited Partnership (a.k.a. Miracle Plus RMB Fund II).

OFAC also issued PAIPA General License 1, "Transactions Authorized Pursuant to the Cyber-Related Sanctions Regulations," and PAIPA General License 2, "Authorizing the Wind Down of Transactions Involving Certain Entities Blocked on October 19, 2026."

articles.headline: OFAC Amends Venezuela-related General License for Earthquake Relief
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has issued Venezuela-related General License 60A, titled "Authorizing Transactions Related to Earthquake Relief Efforts in Venezuela."
This amended general license aims to facilitate humanitarian aid and relief efforts in Venezuela following recent earthquake events.
In conjunction with the general license, OFAC also issued one amended Frequently Asked Question, FAQ 1263, providing further guidance on the authorized transactions.

articles.headline: OFAC Designates Iranian and Cuban Entities, Issues New General Licenses and FAQs
body: The Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) announced new Iran-related designations and a Cuba designation, alongside the issuance of new and amended General Licenses and Frequently Asked Questions.

OFAC issued Russia-related General License 128D, authorizing certain transactions involving Lukoil retail service stations outside Russia, and Russia-related General License 130B, authorizing transactions involving certain Lukoil entities in Bulgaria. Additionally, Iran-related General License FF was issued, authorizing the wind down of transactions involving International Development Bank for Investment and Finance.

The action also included the designation of Cuban state-owned Banco Internacional de Comercio, S.A. (BICSA) and the issuance of a new Cuba-related FAQ (FAQ 1276) and an amended Russia-related FAQ (FAQ 1225).

articles.headline: OFAC Removes Venezuelan National Assembly Head Jorge Jesus Rodriguez Gomez from Sanctions List
body: The U.S. Department of the Treasury's Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) has removed Jorge Jesus Rodriguez Gomez, the head of Venezuela's National Assembly, from its Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List.

The delisting covers five separate entries associated with Rodriguez, including variations of his name, and means he is no longer subject to asset-blocking restrictions. This allows U.S. persons to engage in transactions with him that were previously prohibited, provided no other sanctions apply.

This removal signals a strategic shift in U.S. policy towards Venezuela, moving from punitive economic containment to structured engagement, and follows the earlier delisting of his sister, Delcy Rodriguez.

articles.headline: OFAC Imposes Counter Narcotics and Counter Terrorism Designations

These designations aim to disrupt the financial networks of illicit drug trafficking organizations and terrorist groups, reinforcing U.S. efforts to combat global criminal enterprises.
The updated Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) List reflects these additions, with further details available on the OFAC website.

articles.headline: DHS Adds Three Chinese Genomics Companies to UFLPA Entity List
body: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), on behalf of the Forced Labor Enforcement Task Force (FLETF), announced the addition of three Chinese genomics companies to the Uyghur Forced Labor Prevention Act (UFLPA) Entity List.

Effective October 29, 2026, goods made by BGI Genomics Co., Ltd. (also known as BGI Genomics), MGI Tech Co., Ltd. (also known as MGI), and Shenzhen BGI Technology Co., Ltd. (also known as BGI Group; and BGI Holdings) are prohibited from entering the United States unless importers can demonstrate they were not made with forced labor.

These companies are identified for working with the government of Xinjiang to recruit, transport, transfer, harbor, or receive forced labor or members of persecuted groups out of Xinjiang, and are described as constituting one of the largest advanced gene-sequencing and genetic-material collection enterprises globally, assisting in the region's mass surveillance infrastructure.

articles.headline: Streamlining Export Controls for Drone Exports
body: The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is easing export controls on certain Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs or drones) and related parts, components, accessories, attachments, technology, and software under the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). Specifically, this rule: eliminates wind gust tolerance as a parameter for determining UAV controls under the EAR; increases the threshold for national security controls on certain UAVs from an endurance of 30 minutes to an endurance of 3 hours; makes conforming changes to remove national security controls on software and technology associated with UAVs with an endurance less than 3 hours; maintains military end-use and end-user controls on those lower endurance drones and associated software and technology; clarifies Commerce Control List (CCL) controls for certain UAVs specially designed for military use; and removes national security controls on certain specially designed parts, components, accessories, and attachments for such UAVs as they do not provide any significant military or intelligence capabilities.

articles.headline: Implementation of EAR Export Controls on Silencers, Mufflers, and Sound Suppressors; and Other Firearms Related Changes
body: The Department of Commerce (Commerce), Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is revising the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and the Commerce Control List (CCL) to appropriately control certain silencers, mufflers, and sound suppressors (sound suppressors) that will no longer be described on the International Traffic in Arms Regulations U.S. Munitions List (USML). This interim final rule (IFR) complements a Department of State interim final rule published elsewhere in this issue of the Federal Register (International Traffic in Arms Regulations: USML Category I Firearm Suppressors (1400-AG11) (State IFR)). This transfer of jurisdiction will reduce the regulatory burden on exports of sound suppressors. This IFR also revises the EAR to allow firearms and related items to be temporarily exported and reexported under a license exception as tools of trade, thereby relieving exporters of the regulatory burden of applying for authorization. Finally, this IFR clarifies which items fall within the scope of the EAR's entry clearance requirements for a temporary import.

articles.headline: Enhanced Favorable Treatment for the United Arab Emirates Under the Export Administration Regulations
body: In this final rule, the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) amends the Export Administration Regulations (EAR) to provide enhanced favorable treatment for the United Arab Emirates (UAE). Specifically, BIS is removing the UAE from Country Groups D:3 and D:4 and adding the UAE to Country Group A:5. More license exceptions will now be available, including Strategic Trade Authorization (STA) for the UAE Government and approved commercial entities in the UAE. STA will authorize the export, reexport, or transfer (in-country) of military items; certain commercial satellites and spacecraft; and dual-use items useful in, inter alia, oil and gas production, desalination, and civil nuclear power generation. The UAE Government and approved commercial entities will also have license-free access to advanced computing items, consistent with the May 2025 U.S.-UAE Artificial Intelligence Cooperation framework, without compromising U.S. digital infrastructure buildout.
